definition: A conceptual graph (CG) is a formalism for knowledge representation.
details: In the first published paper on CGs, John F. Sowa used them to represent the conceptual schemas used in database systems. The first book on CGs applied them to a wide range of topics in artificial intelligence, computer science, and cognitive science.

explainer.lead: Conceptual graphs turn knowledge into a structured graph, giving a computer system an explicit representation to work with. John F. Sowa first used them to represent conceptual schemas for database systems, and the approach was subsequently applied across artificial intelligence, computer science, and cognitive science.

tiers.eli5: Imagine showing an idea with boxes and connecting arrows instead of a long sentence. One box might be “Employee,” another “Department,” and the connection might say “works in.” Conceptual graphs use this kind of structured picture to store knowledge in a form a computer can use.
tiers.practitioner: Conceptual graphs can be used to make concepts and their relationships explicit, with database conceptual schemas as their earliest published application. A practical modelling task still requires consistent choices about which concepts and relations belong in the schema. Do not assume that adopting CGs dictates a particular database or application domain.
tiers.paperLevel: A conceptual graph (CG) is a graph-based formalism for knowledge representation. In the first published CG paper, John F. Sowa used CGs to represent conceptual schemas in database systems. The first book on CGs applied the formalism to topics spanning artificial intelligence, computer science, and cognitive science.

explainer.example: For a small organizational schema, represent Employee and Department as concepts and connect them with a works-in relation: Employee → works-in → Department. This graph explicitly captures the relationship that an employee works in a department.

usedIn.name: Database systems
usedIn.detail: Sowa’s first published CG paper used conceptual graphs to represent conceptual schemas.

usedIn.name: Cognitive science
usedIn.detail: Conceptual graphs were among the knowledge-representation approaches applied to cognitive-science topics.

explainer.intuition: A conceptual graph expresses knowledge as connected concepts and relations rather than leaving it buried in prose. The connections make the structure of the represented knowledge explicit.
howItWorks: Choose the knowledge or schema to represent.
Connect concepts with relations that express their roles.
Use the resulting graph as the formal knowledge representation.
explainer.whyItMatters: Conceptual graphs provide a formal way to make the structure of knowledge explicit. Their history connects database schema representation with broader work in AI, computer science, and cognitive science.
misconceptions: A conceptual graph is a formal knowledge-representation method, not merely an informal sketch.
CGs are not restricted to databases, despite their first published application being database conceptual schemas.
